judgments.rationale: The edit correctly incorporates the governing statutory limitation from paragraph (5), which specifies that nothing in the section allows an individual access to information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding, into the access requirement of paragraph (1). The resulting reading is complete, accurate, and independently usable.

The proposed summary erroneously claims that the agency must require every individual, whether accompanied or unaccompanied, to furnish written authorization before access. Under paragraph (1), the agency has discretionary authority ('may require') to require a written statement authorizing discussion only in the accompanying person's presence.

The unchanged draft omits the governing statutory limitation set forth in paragraph (5), which explicitly restricts access under this section for information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding, leaving the reading incomplete for independent use.

source_spans.quote: (d) Access to Records.— Each agency that maintains a system of rec­ords shall—

(1) upon request by any individual to gain access to his record or to any information pertaining to him which is contained in the system, permit him and upon his request, a person of his own choosing to accompany him, to review the record and have a copy made of all or any portion thereof in a form comprehensible to him, except that the agency may require the individual to furnish a written statement authorizing discussion of that individual’s record in the accompanying person’s presence;
(5) nothing in this section shall allow an individual access to any information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding.
